items.title: [reuters.com] Russia's independent Novaya Gazeta to close Nov. 9 under pressure
items.content_html: Novaya Gazeta, one of Russia’s last independent newspapers still operating inside the country, says it will end operations on Nov. 9 after losing access to its Moscow office and reader-donation system. Editor-in-chief Sergei Sokolov said Russian authorities and security services had forced the newsroom to stop working. The paper plans to publish a final issue. The closure follows years of restrictions that intensified after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Authorities revoked the paper’s media licence, blocked its website and designated it a “foreign agent” in September 2026. This month, police searched Sokolov’s home, and investigative reporter Oleg Roldugin was arrested in a criminal case. Novaya Gazeta says the loss of its premises and funding left it unable to continue. Its separately operated sister publication, Novaya Gazeta Europe, will keep publishing from abroad. Founded in 1993, the newspaper became known for investigations into corruption and human-rights abuses. Six of its journalists and contributors were killed, including Anna Politkovskaya, who reported on the Chechen wars.

items.title: [theguardian.com] China expels 33 senior officials as Xi tightens party discipline
items.content_html: China’s ruling Communist Party expelled 33 senior officials at the close of a four-day leadership meeting in Beijing on Oct. 29, confirming the removal of former senior military commander Zhang Youxia, former Xinjiang party chief Ma Xingrui and others. Sixteen of those expelled were from the military. The party’s communiqué cited serious disciplinary and legal violations without detailing individual allegations. Only 279 of the 376 full and alternate Central Committee members appointed in 2022 attended — the lowest attendance at a plenum under President Xi Jinping, with a record number of empty seats. Purges have reduced the seven-member Central Military Commission, which commands China’s armed forces, to Xi and General Zhang Shengmin, a military anti-corruption official. The party promoted Zhang Shengmin to the Politburo at the meeting. The meeting focused on internal discipline and anti-corruption, while analysts differ on whether the drive chiefly addresses graft or reinforces Xi’s authority. The party also confirmed that its 21st congress will take place in Beijing in the second half of 2027, when it will reshuffle its leadership and Xi is widely expected to seek a fourth term.

items.content_html: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado returned to Caracas after nearly 10 months in exile and said Thursday that presidential elections should be held in 2027, citing a transition plan outlined by U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio. She said her own team, not a government, arranged her return and thanked President Donald Trump’s administration for capturing former President Nicolás Maduro in January. Interim President Delcy Rodríguez also said elections would be held but set no date. She said they would follow reforms and be organized by a renewed electoral authority. Machado said she had received no message from Rodríguez and is not part of Washington-backed talks between the government and opposition factions, though she wants the talks to succeed. Machado’s party is excluded from the talks, which are addressing changes to the Supreme Court and electoral council. U.S. officials have said Rodríguez should leave office in 2027 after those reforms. Machado also criticized a U.S.-Venezuela oil agreement for lacking transparency.

items.title: [euronews.com] Lagarde exit opens ECB succession as French borrowing costs rise
items.content_html: European Central Bank policymakers held the deposit rate at 2.5% on Oct. 29, but President Christine Lagarde said they had seriously discussed a rate increase as energy prices and bond yields tightened financing conditions for households and businesses. Eurozone inflation reached 3.8% in September, and average 10-year government bond yields had risen about 35 basis points since the ECB’s September forecast. France’s 10-year borrowing cost topped 5% last week for the first time since 2002. The same day, Lagarde said she would leave the Frankfurt-based central bank on Feb. 7, 2027, before the end of her eight-year term, saying she wanted to speak on issues beyond monetary policy. Her departure opens a contest to lead the institution that sets interest rates across the euro area. Markets showed little reaction to the announcement, with analysts saying the ECB’s established practices were likely to outlast its president. Investors were pricing in three further rate increases by the end of 2027, which would bring the deposit rate to 3.25%. The ECB’s next policy meeting is scheduled for Dec. 17.

items.title: [lemonde.fr] Spain train crash kills 68 as investigators probe control error
items.content_html: A Renfe high-speed train struck a stationary Iryo train near Urda in central Spain on Oct. 28, killing at least 68 people and injuring 107, including 15 in serious condition. The two trains, travelling from Madrid toward Seville, carried a total of 544 passengers. It was Spain’s second deadly high-speed rail crash this year, following a January collision near Adamuz that killed 46. Transport Minister Óscar Puente said a computer failure disabled the LZB safety system on a 63-kilometre stretch at about 8:30 a.m., stopping six trains. He said Madrid’s control centre then authorized the Renfe train to resume at normal speed; it travelled about 25 kilometres before hitting the stopped Iryo train at 8:53 a.m. Puente called the instruction “inexplicable” and said the drivers were not at fault. Iryo said its train had not been authorized to restart and remained stopped after the signal failure, according to ABC News Australia. Investigators are examining the differing accounts. Spain declared three days of national mourning, from Oct. 29 through 31. The Rail Accident Investigation Commission and judicial authorities are investigating. Rail services between Madrid, Ciudad Real and Andalusia were suspended.

items.title: [cbc.ca] Liberals defeat Conservative bill to repeal B.C. tanker ban
items.content_html: Canada’s Liberal government defeated a Conservative bill Wednesday to repeal the oil tanker ban on British Columbia’s northern coast, leaving the restrictions in place. The law bars tankers from carrying more than 12,500 metric tonnes of crude oil in the covered coastal area. Conservatives cited Calgary-based Strathcona Resources’ proposal to move as many as 250,000 barrels of oil a day by rail through Prince Rupert for export. Prime Minister Mark Carney agreed with British Columbia earlier this summer to maintain the ban. He and Alberta Premier Danielle Smith subsequently announced a proposed pipeline route to the south that would comply with it. Smith supported repeal. The bill’s defeat at second reading means it will not proceed to committee.

items.title: [The Guardian Global Development] How rebuilding old mosques is bringing Sikhs, Hindus and Muslims together in Punjab
items.content_html:
🪶 🌲 🏔️ ✏️

Many Muslims saw their places of worship destroyed or abandoned during the sectarian violence of India’s partition in 1947. Now villagers of many faiths are coming together to revive them

Gajju Khan is smiling as he sits in an unfinished building in the northern Indian state of Punjab in the late afternoon. The 87-year-old is hopeful that before he dies he will hear the azaan, the Muslim call to prayer, echo across his village once again when the mosque is completed.

The last time he heard it here was when he was eight years old, living with his parents in Tira Maloya, a village in Chandigarh, not far from where he lives now.

Bibi Rajinder Kaur, a Sikh, donated family land to build a mosque in her village. ‘There is no deed better than giving someone a place to worship,’ she says

items.title: [cbc.ca] B.C. animal rescuer Jesse Adams killed by drone in Ukraine
items.content_html:
🪶 🏔️ ✏️

Jesse Adams, the 41-year-old co-founder of Vancouver Island’s RainCoast Dog Rescue Society, died Oct. 25 after a Russian first-person-view drone struck the vehicle he was using to evacuate animals in Kramatorsk, eastern Ukraine. Animal Rescue Kharkiv said Adams suffered severe injuries and died after emergency surgery. Adams had been volunteering with Animal Rescue Kharkiv since May and had travelled to Ukraine repeatedly to help evacuate animals from areas near the front line. The organization said hundreds of animals were alive because of his work. While abroad, he continued taking calls and arranging adoptions for RainCoast in British Columbia, according to Victoria Humane Society executive director Penny Stone.
